comment: This changes the width handling from an explicit `if self.width:` check to a truthiness check on the constructor argument. As a result, passing `width=0` (or any other falsy numeric value) will no longer be treated as an explicit width request and will instead fall back to `scale(unit_size)`. That is a correctness regression because the caller’s requested width is ignored. The previous implementation distinguished `None` from a provided value via `self.width`, so the new code should preserve that behavior by checking `if width is not None:` rather than relying on truthiness.
